title: Spring Boot: spring.mongodb.password containing a space reaches the driver as '+' and authentication fails

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue/PR; short error excerpt quoted.

symptom: A MongoDB account whose password contains a space (for example 'my secret') cannot authenticate when configured through spring.mongodb.username and spring.mongodb.password, although the same account works in mongosh. The credentials handed to the driver contain 'my+secret'.
cause: PropertiesMongoConnectionDetails builds a connection string and encodes username and password with URLEncoder.encode, which turns a space into '+'. The MongoDB driver's ConnectionString treats '+' as a literal plus sign, not a space, so the password changes.
fixSummary: Provide the credentials in spring.mongodb.uri with the space percent-encoded as %20, for example mongodb://audit-writer:my%20secret@mongo.internal.example:27017/audit?authSource=admin (keep host, database and authSource unchanged). Defining your own MongoConnectionDetails bean that encodes with %20 works too. Fixed in Boot 4.0.9.
